fields.title: Canada Study Permit (Student Visa) from India: Fees and Steps
fields.summary: What you need for a Canada study permit from India: the CAD 150 fee, documents, PAL rules for master's students, work hours and the post-graduation work permit.
fields.seo_title: Canada Student Visa from India: Study Permit Fees & Steps
fields.meta_description: Canada study permit for Indian students: CAD 150 fee, documents, PAL rule for master's students, 24-hour work limit and the 3-year post-graduation permit.
fields.body_md:
## The short answer

- **Permit:** a **study permit** lets you study at a **designated learning institution (DLI)**. A DLI is a school approved by a province or territory to host international students. You apply online.
- **Visa:** if you need a visitor visa to enter Canada, IRCC issues it with your permit. You do not apply for it or pay for it separately.
- **Fees:** the study permit costs **CAD 150** (**₹9,791**). Biometrics cost **CAD 85** (**₹5,548**). Together that is **CAD 235** (**₹15,338**).
- **Money to show:** your first-year tuition, travel, and **CAD 23,448** for living costs (**₹15.30 lakh**) if you apply on or after 1 September 2026. Read the full sum in our [proof of funds guide](/study-abroad/study-in/canada/canada-proof-of-funds-guide).
- **PAL:** a master's student at a public DLI does not need a provincial attestation letter (PAL) since 1 January 2026. Quebec asks for a different document, the CAQ.
- **Work:** up to **24 hours a week** off campus while your classes are running.
- **After your degree:** a post-graduation work permit (PGWP) of up to **3 years** for a master's, if you score **CLB 7** in all four language areas.

Rupee amounts use **₹65.27 per Canadian dollar**, the Bank of Canada rate for 27 November 2026. Rates move every day and your bank will charge its own rate, so treat the rupee figures as a guide.

## Before you apply

You cannot apply for a study permit until your school sends you a **letter of acceptance (LOA)**. IRCC says: "You can't apply for a study permit until you have your LOA." Apply to your programme early. Check each university's own deadline on its page in our [Canada section](/study-abroad/study-in/canada).

IRCC asks your school to check that your LOA is valid. If the school does not reply by the deadline, IRCC returns your application and refunds your processing fee. Ask your school to confirm it will do this before you apply.

## Documents you need

IRCC lists these documents for most applicants:

- **Letter of acceptance:** always required.
- **Proof of identity:** a valid passport and two recent passport-size photos.
- **Proof of funds:** always required. See our [proof of funds guide](/study-abroad/study-in/canada/canada-proof-of-funds-guide).
- **PAL or CAQ:** needed in most cases. Master's students at public DLIs are exempt from the PAL, but must show proof that they are exempt. See the next section.
- **Letter of explanation:** IRCC marks this as recommended. Explain why you want to study in Canada and that you understand your duties as an international student.
- **Medical exam:** you may need one if you plan to stay in Canada for more than 6 months.
- **Police certificate:** IRCC may ask for one. Apply early if you think you need it.
- **Local instructions:** your local visa office may ask for other documents. Select your country on the IRCC page to see them.

## Do you need a PAL?

A **provincial attestation letter (PAL)** is a letter from a province that confirms there is a place for you. IRCC says that since **1 January 2026**, some students do not need one. These are students in a master's or doctoral degree programme at a **public** DLI. You still need your LOA and the other documents.

If you do not provide a PAL, you must provide proof that you meet one of the exceptions. Ask your school what proof it can give you.

Other students usually do need a PAL, including most undergraduate and college students. You get it from your school. IRCC says it must go in with your application, not after. A PAL is valid only for the year it was issued. A 2026 PAL runs to **31 December 2026**, and you cannot use it for a later cap year.

IRCC set a cap of **309,670** application spaces for 2026 for students who need a PAL. IRCC has not published 2027 provincial allocations as of 28 November 2026. If your school is private or your programme is not a master's, ask the school how this will affect your application.

## Studying in Quebec

Quebec asks for a **Quebec Acceptance Certificate (CAQ)** from the Government of Quebec. IRCC says most students who do not need a PAL must still get a CAQ. Your school will tell you how to apply. Quebec also sets its own money rule: **CAD 24,617** for one person (**₹16.07 lakh**) for applications from 1 January 2026.

## Steps to apply

1. Get your LOA from the university.
2. Check whether you need a PAL, or whether you are exempt. In Quebec, get your CAQ.
3. Collect your passport, photos, proof of funds and letter of explanation.
4. Apply online through your IRCC account and pay the fees. IRCC says you must apply online.
5. Give your fingerprints and photo when IRCC sends you the letter. You have **30 days** from the date on the letter.
6. Wait for the decision. If you are approved, IRCC issues your documents.

## Fees

| Fee | CAD | In rupees |
|---|---|---|
| Study permit, per person | **CAD 150** | ₹9,791 |
| Biometrics, per person | **CAD 85** | ₹5,548 |
| Biometrics, family of 2 or more, maximum | **CAD 170** | ₹11,096 |

You only need to give biometrics once every **10 years**. You may also pay a third party for a medical exam, police certificate or language test. IRCC does not publish those amounts on the pages we checked.

## How long it takes

IRCC's study permit page says the processing time "varies by country". It gives no fixed time. Use the processing times tool on the IRCC site, and apply early. We do not give a number here because IRCC does not give one for India on the pages we read.

The Student Direct Stream, a faster route that India was part of, **ended on 8 November 2024**. Today every applicant goes through the regular study permit stream.

## Work while you study

You can work **up to 24 hours a week** off campus while classes run. You must be a full-time student at a DLI. Your programme must be at least 6 months long and lead to a degree. Your permit must carry the work condition. You also need a social insurance number (SIN). You can only start working once your programme starts.

During breaks that your school schedules, you can work unlimited hours. Working more than 24 hours a week while classes run breaks your permit conditions. You can lose your student status for it.

From **1 April 2026**, eligible post-secondary students no longer need a separate work permit for co-op placements and internships that their programme requires.

## After your degree

A **post-graduation work permit (PGWP)** lets you work in Canada after you graduate. For a master's degree, IRCC says you can get a **3-year** PGWP. Your programme must be at least **8 months** long. It can be shorter than 2 years.

You must prove your English or French with at least **CLB 7** in all four language areas. CLB means Canadian Language Benchmarks. There is no field-of-study rule for a master's degree. You must apply within **180 days** of getting confirmation that you finished. You must also have studied full-time in each term, except your last.

faq_json.q: How much is the Canada study permit fee for Indian students?
faq_json.a: The study permit costs CAD 150, about ₹9,791 at ₹65.27 per Canadian dollar. Biometrics cost another CAD 85, about ₹5,548.

faq_json.q: Do I need a separate visa to study in Canada?
faq_json.a: No separate application. IRCC says that if you need a visa or an eTA, it issues it with your study permit and charges no other fee.

faq_json.q: Do I need a PAL for a master's in Canada?
faq_json.a: Not for a master's or doctoral degree at a public designated learning institution, since 1 January 2026. You must still show proof that you are exempt. Quebec asks for a CAQ.

faq_json.q: How many hours can I work on a study permit?
faq_json.a: Up to 24 hours a week off campus while classes run, and unlimited hours in breaks your school schedules. You need the work condition on your permit and a SIN.

faq_json.q: How long is the post-graduation work permit after a master's?
faq_json.a: Up to 3 years if your programme was at least 8 months long. You need CLB 7 in all four language areas and must apply within 180 days.

faq_json.q: Can I still use the Student Direct Stream from India?
faq_json.a: No. IRCC ended the Student Direct Stream on 8 November 2024. All applicants now use the regular study permit stream.
